_about: Dialogue templates. Each key holds variants: a string, or {t, traits, mood, emote}. Variants tagged with traits are preferred for NPCs who have one of them and never used for NPCs who have none; mood is 'good' (mood >= 65) or 'bad' (mood < 35). Variables: {raka} how this NPC addresses Raka, {name} NPC's name, {first} name without title, {greet} Pagi/Siang/Sore/Malam, {topic}, {other}, {place}, {heading}, {detail}, {job}, {item} a gift's name.
intro.generic: {greet}. You must be {raka}, Mbah Minah's grandson. I'm {name}.
Oh! The new face on Gang Mawar. {name}. Welcome back to Sukamaju.
So you're the one who moved into Mbah Minah's house. I'm {name}, pleased to meet you.
{greet}, {raka}. Everyone's been talking about you. I'm {name}.
Ah, Mbah Minah's cucu! I'm {name}. The kampung's been waiting to meet you.
npc.bambang.intro: Raka! Finally. Pak Bambang, the RT here. Your grandmother kept this whole gang in line, you know. Don't forget to bring your KTP to my house so I can register you as a resident.
npc.bambang.story: I spent thirty years counting other people's money at the bank. Now I count potholes and sign letters. It's better work, honestly.
Your grandmother talked me into standing for RT. She said, 'Bambang, you complain the most, so you should fix things.' Hard to argue with Mbah Minah.
npc.ratna.intro: Oh, you're Raka! I'm Bu Ratna, Pak RT's wife. Have you eaten? You look thin. I'll bring you some kue lapis later.
npc.ratna.story: I run the arisan for the ibu-ibu. Twelve women, one pot of money, and a great deal of opinion.
My kue lapis recipe came from my mother. Nine layers, and each one steamed on its own. People think it's easy. It isn't.
npc.sri.intro: So this is Mbah Minah's cucu! I'm Bu Sri, this is my warung. If you need rice, gas, pulsa or news, you come here first.
npc.sri.story: My husband opened this warung twenty years ago. He passed when Dimas was small, and I've kept it open every day since. Even Lebaran, for an hour.
Your grandmother bought her tea here every single morning. Teh tubruk, two spoons of sugar. I still reach for the jar at seven.
npc.dimas.intro: Oh, uh, hi. Dimas. My mum runs the warung. You're... Kak Raka, right? The one from the city?
npc.dimas.story: I play futsal at the lapangan every afternoon. We never win against the RW 05 team, but one day.
Mum wants me to take over the warung. I kind of want to be a mechanic like Bang Udin. Don't tell her.
npc.darto.intro: Raka? Raka! The boy who broke my window with a kite! Hah. Look at you now. Pak Darto, if you've forgotten.
npc.darto.story: I built half the doors on this gang with these hands. Jati wood, no nails where I could help it. Most of them are still standing.
Your grandmother and I used to argue about everything. Politics, football, the price of chilli. I miss the arguments more than I'd admit.
npc.sumi.intro: Masya Allah, Raka, you've grown! I'm Bu Darto. You used to hide under our table when Minah called you for your bath.
npc.sumi.story: Minah and I walked to the pasar together every morning for forty years. Now I go alone and still save her a place in the queue.
We had no children of our own, so every child on this gang was a little bit ours. You included.
npc.yusuf.intro: Eh, Mas Raka! Yusuf. I drive ojek from the pangkalan by the gate. You need a ride anywhere, you call me, special price for neighbours.
npc.yusuf.story: Before the ojek I worked in a factory in Cikarang. Twelve-hour shifts. Now I'm my own boss, even if the boss pays badly.
My wife Lestari cooks for half the offices in town. Honestly, the catering pays more than my motor does.
npc.lestari.intro: Hello, Mas Raka. Lestari, Mas Yusuf's wife. I do home catering, nasi box, snack boxes. If you ever need an order for work, I'll give you the neighbour price.
npc.lestari.story: I started with ten boxes of nasi kuning for a wedding. Last month I did three hundred for a company event. My kitchen is still the same size.
I want to sell online, with photos and a proper menu. I just don't know how to make it look nice. You're a designer, aren't you?
npc.bima.intro: Kak! Are you the new person? I'm Bima. I can do twenty keepy-uppies. Wanna see?
npc.bima.story: I'm gonna play for Persib when I grow up. Or be an astronaut. Or both.
There's a big fish in the kali. I've almost caught it three times. Bapak says it's a sandal but it moved.
npc.putri.intro: ...Hi. I'm Putri. My mama makes nasi box.
npc.putri.story: I have a cat. She's orange. She's not really mine, she just sleeps on our teras.
When I'm big I'm going to have a warung like Bu Sri but only for sweets.
npc.slamet.intro: Mas Raka! Slamet, Warkop Berkah's mine. First kopi is on the house for new neighbours. Second one you pay, hehe.
npc.slamet.story: I opened the warkop so the men would have somewhere to argue that isn't their wives' kitchen. Public service, really.
The TV was a present from the whole gang, for the 2010 World Cup. It's older than some of my customers.
npc.hartono.intro: Hm. Raka, isn't it. Hartono. I was at the kelurahan office for thirty-two years, so if your papers are wrong, I will know.
npc.hartono.story: I kept the kampung's records by hand before the computers came. Births, deaths, weddings. I could tell you who lived in your house in 1978.
People think I'm a grumpy old man because I like quiet. I am a grumpy old man. But the quiet is a separate matter.
npc.joko.intro: Mas Raka! Joko, Bakso Mas Joko. You can hear my cart before you see it. Come by the pos ronda in the evening, first bowl half price.
npc.joko.story: My bapak pushed a bakso cart for thirty years. Same bell, same recipe. I just added more chilli.
The secret to bakso is the broth, not the balls. Everyone thinks it's the balls. It's the broth.
npc.udin.intro: Yo. Udin. I fix motors. If yours makes a noise it shouldn't, bring it to me. If it makes no noise, also bring it to me.
npc.udin.story: I learned engines at a bengkel in Bekasi when I was fifteen. Never went back to school. Never needed to.
Some people here complain I'm loud. A motor has to be tested. You can't test a motor quietly.
npc.rahmat.intro: Oh, excuse me, Mas. Rahmat. I work nights, security at a mall. So if I look half asleep, that's why.
npc.rahmat.story: Night shift is peaceful. Just me, the cameras and a flask of coffee. People forget the city has a quiet side.
I send most of my pay home to Garut, to my mother. One day I'll build her a proper kitchen.
npc.yati.intro: Aduh, so you're Raka! I'm Bu Yati, I do sewing. If you need your trousers taken in, and you do, come see me.
npc.yati.story: I've sewn the wedding kebaya for half the brides in this RW. I remember every measurement. Every single one.
My Fajar spends all day on his phone making videos. I said, make a video of your mother's sewing. He said nobody wants that. Rude.
npc.endang.intro: You're the grandson! Endang. I rent rooms to students, Mas Rizky and Mbak Nadia. So if you hear music at night, it's not me.
npc.endang.story: I started renting rooms after my husband left. Students are better tenants than husbands. They pay on time, mostly.
I know it looks like I know everyone's business. I only know the business people tell me. Which is everyone's.
npc.wati.intro: Assalamualaikum. I'm Bu Wati. I sell jamu. You look tired, Mas. Kunyit asam tomorrow, I'll save you a bottle.
npc.wati.story: My grandmother taught me every root and leaf. Kencur, temulawak, sirih. The pharmacy sells the same thing in a plastic box for ten times the price.
I walk to three kampungs every morning with the basket on my back. Twenty years. My knees have opinions about it now.
npc.rizky.intro: Oh, hey, Mas. Rizky. I rent a room at Bu Endang's. Informatics, fifth semester. If your wifi breaks, I'm the guy.
npc.rizky.story: I'm building an app for the RT. Announcements, ronda schedules, arisan reminders. Pak RT says he prefers the loudspeaker.
I'm from Padang originally. I miss my mum's rendang. Nobody here makes it right. Don't tell Bu Sri.
npc.nadia.intro: Hi! Nadia. Design student, so I've heard you're a real designer. Freelance? That's the dream.
npc.nadia.story: I sketch the kampung on weekends. The gang rooftops from the bridge are my favourite. All those terracotta angles.
My parents want me to be a civil servant. I want to design book covers. We've agreed to stop talking about it.
npc.hasan.intro: Assalamualaikum, Mas Raka. I'm Hasan, I look after the musholla. Your grandmother paid for our carpets, did you know? The door is always open.
npc.hasan.story: I came here as a young teacher twenty years ago for one year. The kampung didn't let me leave.
People bring me their problems more than their prayers. I think that's all right. Sometimes they're the same thing.
npc.karyo.intro: Mas Raka! Karyo, tukang. I've seen your grandmother's roof from the gang. That needs work before the rainy season. When you're ready, call me.
npc.karyo.story: I can fix anything with a roof, a pipe or a wire. My own house, though, the tap has been dripping for two years.
Mbah Minah hired me for my first real job, a new kitchen door. She paid me double and said, 'Now do the next one properly.'
npc.ayu.intro: Hi, Mas Raka, I'm Ayu. I work from home, customer service, headset on all day. Sorry if I look distracted, I usually am.
npc.ayu.story: My husband works on a ship, so it's just me and the baby most months. The neighbours have been wonderful.
Eight hours of angry customers on the phone, then I sit on the lapangan bench and listen to the kids. Best therapy there is.
npc.fajar.intro: Bro! Kak Raka? Fajar. I do content. Kampung life, street food, that kind of thing. Can I film you later? You'd be great for engagement.
npc.fajar.story: My video of Mas Joko's bakso got eleven thousand views. Eleven thousand! He still doesn't know what views are.
Mum wants me to go to university. I want to go viral first. Then university. Maybe.
greet.stranger: {greet}. How are you finding the kampung?

greet.stranger.t: Oh! {greet}, {raka}! Nice to see you out and about!
{greet}! So, what brings you round here? Tell me everything.

greet.acquaintance: {greet}! Nice to see a familiar face.
Oh, {raka}. Mampir? Stop for a bit.

greet.acquaintance.t: {raka}! {greet}! Come, come, I've got something to tell you.
{greet}. Not the best day, to be honest.

greet.friend: Eh, {raka}! I was just thinking about you.
{greet}, {raka}. Sit down, you look like you need a rest.
{raka}! Just the person I wanted to see.

greet.friend.t: Hmph. {greet}, {raka}. You're the only one on this gang who makes sense.
{greet}, {raka}. It's been a long day, but it's better now.

greet.again: Oh, {raka}, again! Did you forget something?
Twice in one day, {raka}. People will talk.

greet.again.t: Hehe, you again! I don't mind.

greet.busy: Oh, {raka}! I'm on my way to {heading}, but I've got a minute.
{greet}, {raka}. Walk with me? I'm heading to {heading}.
Oh, hello! I was just going to {heading}.

greet.busy.t: I'm busy, {raka}. Going to {heading}. What is it?

greet.memory.topic_like: {raka}! I keep thinking about our chat about {topic}.
Oh, {raka}, you know, after we talked about {topic} I couldn't stop thinking about it.
greet.memory.tease_bad: Oh. {raka}. I haven't forgotten what you said, you know.
{greet}. I hope you're in a kinder mood today.
Hm. Here to make fun of me again?
{raka}. That remark of yours the other day wasn't very nice.
{greet}. Let's keep it polite today, shall we?
greet.memory.joke_good: {raka}! I told your joke to everyone at {place}. Hehe.
{greet}! Got any more jokes like the last one?
Hah, {raka}! I'm still laughing about that joke.
{greet}, {raka}. You made my week with that joke.
greet.memory.compliment: {greet}, {raka}. You were so kind the other day.
Oh, {raka}! You always say such nice things.
Ah, {raka}. Thank you again for what you said.
{greet}, {raka}. You've got a good heart, like your grandmother.
greet.memory.first: Ah, the new neighbour again. How's the house?
{raka}! Good to see you again so soon.
{greet}. Remember me? We met the other day.
address.proper.elder: {greet} to you too, Nak. Such good manners. Minah raised you well.
Ah, you remember how to greet your elders. Good, good.
{greet} to you too, Nak. Polite young man.
Hm! Proper manners. We don't see enough of that anymore.
Ah, pleasant. Most young people just nod at me these days.

address.proper.elder.t: Hm. At least someone still knows how to greet properly.

address.proper.peer: {greet}! You don't have to be so formal, you know.
address.proper.young: {greet}! You called me Dek, like my uncle does.
address.casual.rude: {first}? Just {first}? Hm. In my day we said Pak, or Bu.
I'm old enough to be your parent, {raka}. A little respect.
Hm. Mbah Minah would have pinched your ear for that.
That's not how you greet your elders, Nak.
Just '{first}', is it? You've been in the city too long.
address.casual.meh: Oh, er, hi. It's {name}, actually. Hehe.
Hi... We're not that close yet, are we?
Hey. Bit casual, but all right.
topic.like.football: Football! Don't get me started on Persib this season. Actually, do. Get me started.
Did you watch the match last night? That second goal! I nearly knocked Pak Slamet's TV over.
Football's the only thing that gets the whole warkop quiet. Then very loud.
The lapangan futsal league starts next month. RW 05 better be scared.
My whole week depends on the weekend's result. Is that healthy? No. Do I care? Also no.
topic.like.food: Food! Now you're talking. Have you tried Bu Sri's nasi uduk? No? What have you been eating?
The best thing in this kampung is Mas Joko's bakso after the rain. Trust me.
I could talk about sambal all day. There's a correct amount of terasi and most people get it wrong.
Food is how this kampung says it loves you. If someone brings you a plate, you bring it back full.
Ah, food. I was just thinking about gorengan. I'm always thinking about gorengan.
topic.like.family: Family's everything. You're lucky, your grandmother's house kept you close to all of us.
My family drives me mad, but I'd do anything for them. You know how it is.
Every Lebaran the whole family squeezes into one small house. Loudest, happiest day of the year.
I love talking about family. Remind me to show you the photos. All three hundred of them.
Family is the ones who bring you soup when you're sick, blood or not.
topic.like.work: Ah, you want to hear about my work? Nobody ever asks! Sit down.
Work's been busy, but the good kind of busy. I like being useful.
People think my job is simple. It's not. Let me explain the whole thing.
I'm proud of what I do. It's not glamorous, but the kampung needs it.
Honestly, I love my work. On most days. Some days less.
topic.like.kampung news: Did you hear? Pak RT wants to repaint the gapura before 17 Agustus. Red and white, of course.
Kampung news! The drain on Gang Melati is finally getting fixed. Only took three years of meetings.
There's talk of a new minimarket on the main road. Bu Sri is not happy about it.
The RT meeting was so long last week, Pak Hartono fell asleep. Twice.
Kerja bakti this Sunday, you know. Everyone's going. You're going. Aren't you?
topic.like.weather: The weather! It's been so hot. The rain always comes the moment you hang your washing.
You can smell the rain before it comes here. Wet dust. Best smell in the world.
Rainy season's coming. The kali will rise, the frogs will sing, and every roof will leak.
When it rains in the afternoon everyone ends up under the warung roof. Best conversations happen then.
I check the sky every morning like my father did. More accurate than the phone.
topic.like.motorbikes: Motors! Now that's a topic. A good bebek engine will outlive us all.
My first motor was a Honda Astrea older than me. Pushed it more than I rode it. Loved it.
Everyone here has an opinion on motors. Most of them are wrong, but they're passionate about it.
You can tell a lot about a man by how he treats his motor.
The sound of a well-tuned motor in the morning. That's music.
topic.like.old days: The old days! When I was young this whole gang was rice fields. Frogs everywhere.
Before the jalan was paved, we'd come home muddy to the knees. Our mothers were furious.
Your grandmother used to organise the whole 17 Agustus by herself. Sack races, panjat pinang, everything.
The old days weren't all good, but they were quieter. We knew every face.
I remember when the first television came to this kampung. The whole RT crowded into one living room.
topic.like.religion: The musholla's been full for Maghrib lately. It's good to see the young ones coming.
Ramadan's not far off. I'm already planning the bukber menu for the musholla.
Pengajian on Thursday nights, you should come. Ustadz Hasan explains things so gently.
I find a lot of peace in the adzan. It gives the day its shape.
Every Ramadan the whole kampung wakes up for sahur together. The kids bang on pots at three in the morning.
topic.like.music: Music! I love dangdut, and I'm not ashamed of it. Rhoma Irama is a poet.
Someone plays guitar at the pos ronda some nights. Out of tune, but lovely.
I've got a playlist for everything. Cooking, cleaning, being sad. Mostly being sad.
Do you play anything? We need more musicians for the 17 Agustus stage.
Music makes the work go faster. Everyone knows that.
topic.like.market prices: Don't talk to me about the price of chilli! It doubled in a week. A week!
Eggs are up again. At this rate I'll have to keep chickens.
The trick at the pasar is to go late, when they want to go home. Half price, and they're happy to see you.
I track every price in my head. Rice, oil, onions. Ask me anything.
Prices go up like a kite and come down like a feather. That's what my mother used to say.
topic.like.gossip: Well, since you ask... someone on Gang Kenanga has a new motor, and nobody knows where the money came from.
Did you see who was walking home late from the warkop last night? No? Well, I did.
I don't gossip. I just share information. Loudly. With everyone.
Ooh, there's so much going on. Where do I even start?
Everyone says Bu Endang knows everything. She learned it all from me.
topic.neutral: Oh, {topic}. I don't know much about it, but go on.
Hm, {topic}. Not really my thing, but it's nice to chat.
Ah, {topic}. People seem to like that.

topic.neutral.t: Oh, {topic}! Hehe, I don't know much, but tell me more!

topic.dislike: Ugh, {topic}. Can we talk about something else?
Please, not {topic}. I get enough of that at home.
Hm. I'd rather not talk about {topic}.
topic.repeat: {topic} again? You really like that, huh.
Again? Let's talk about something new.

topic.repeat.t: Are you listening at all? We did {topic}.

ask.like: Me? Honestly, I could talk about {topic} for hours.
What do I like? {topic}. No question.
Hehe, if you want to make me happy, bring up {topic}.
You want to know me? Start with {topic}.
ask.dislike: I'll tell you what I can't stand. {topic}. Please don't ever.
Just don't get me started on {topic}. Not in a good way.
Honestly? {topic} drives me up the wall.
Whatever you do, don't talk to me about {topic}.
ask.birthday: My birthday? {detail}. Not that anyone remembers.
It's {detail}. My family makes nasi kuning every year.
{detail}. Why, are you planning something? Hehe.
ask.done: You know me well enough by now, {raka}. Ask me something else another day.
Hehe, that's enough about me for today.
There's not much more to tell. Let's talk about you some time.
You've heard all my stories for today.
Later, later. I'm not that interesting.

ask.done.t: Enough questions. What am I, a census?

compliment.good: Oh, stop it. Actually, don't stop.
That's so nice of you to say.
Hehe, your grandmother was a sweet talker too.

compliment.good.t: Wah, really? Thank you, thank you!

compliment.shy: You don't have to say that... but thank you.
Oh, I don't know about that. But thank you.

compliment.flat.t: Save the sweet talk for someone who needs it.

compliment.repeat: Twice in one day? Now I'm suspicious.
You're laying it on a bit thick.
joke.good: Hahaha! Oh, that's a good one. I'm stealing that.
Hah! Where did you hear that?
Hah! You're funnier than you look, {raka}.

joke.good.t: ...Hm. Heh. All right, that was funny.

joke.flat: I think I've heard that one before.
joke.bad: Hm. I don't laugh at that sort of thing.
Is that what passes for a joke in the city?
Please don't say that in front of the children.
tease.good: Hah! Look who's talking! You can't even ride a motor.
Oi! Watch it, city boy. Hehe.
Hahaha, cheeky! Just like when you were small.
Ooh, you'll pay for that one. Hehe.
tease.bad: Excuse me? We're not that close, {raka}.
Is that how they talk in the city?
gossip.good: {other}? Oh, a good person. Always the first to help.
I like {other}. You can trust that one.
{other} is one of the good ones. Heart of gold.
Between you and me, {other} is my favourite person on this gang.
{other}? We go way back. Solid as a teak door.
gossip.bad: {other}? Don't get me started. Let's just say we don't see eye to eye.
Between us, {raka}, I'd keep my distance from {other}.
{other}. Hmph. Some people should pay back what they owe.
I'm not saying anything about {other}. But if I were, it wouldn't be nice.
{other} and I have... history. Leave it at that.
gossip.neutral: {other}? Nothing much to say. Nice enough.
Oh, {other}'s all right. Why do you ask?
{other}? We say hello. That's about it.
gossip.refuse: I don't talk about people behind their backs, {raka}.
Ask them yourself. That's my advice.
Gossip is a sin, you know. Well, nearly.
No, no. I stay out of other people's business.
If you want gossip, go to the warung. Not me.
gossip.shy: Oh, I don't really... I don't know people that well yet.
Um, maybe when we know each other better.
I don't know you well enough for that, hehe.
bye.warm: Mampir lagi, ya, {raka}! Come by again.
Say hello to your grandmother's house for me. Hehe.
greet.memory.gift_loved: {raka}! I'm still thinking about that {item}. Terima kasih, ya.
Oh, it's you! That {item} was just what I needed.
{greet}, {raka}. You spoil me with {item} like that.
Ah, the one who brought me {item}! Come, sit.
{greet}! Everyone asked where I got that {item}. I said, my neighbour!
gift.loved: {item}! For me? Oh, {raka}, how did you know?
Aduh, {item}! My favourite. You shouldn't have. But I'm glad you did.
{item}! You've been asking around about me, haven't you? Hehe. Thank you.
Oh! {item}. This is exactly what I wanted. Terima kasih banyak.
Masya Allah, {item}! You've made my whole week.

gift.loved.t: Hm. {item}. ...Well. This is very good. Thank you, {raka}.
Oh... {item}? For me? Th-thank you so much.

gift.dish: You cooked this? {item}, from your own kitchen! Now you're a real kampung neighbour.
Berbagi, just like Mbah Minah used to. {item}, how lovely. I'll bring your plate back full.
Oh, you made {item} for me? That's the kindest thing. Terima kasih.
{item}, still warm! Your grandmother would be proud.

gift.dish.t: Hm. You made this? ...It smells right. I'll eat it later. Thank you.

gift.liked: Oh, {item}! That's very nice of you.
Oh, thank you! {item} is always welcome.
gift.neutral: Hehe, {item}. That's a funny thing to give someone. Thanks.
Oh, {item}. I'll find a use for it.

gift.neutral.t: {item}? What am I supposed to do with that?

gift.disliked: Oh. {item}. I, um, don't really like that.
{item}? Hm. That's not really for me, {raka}.
{item}. I'm sorry, I can't stand the stuff.

gift.disliked.t: Oh... {item}. Hehe. Thank you... I think.

gift.again: Another one? No, no, you've given me enough today.
{raka}, one gift a day is plenty! Keep it for someone else.
Hehe, you're too generous. Save it.
You already brought me something today. Put that away.
Aduh, stop! Give it to one of the other neighbours.
greet.callout: There he is! I thought you'd walk right past me.
{raka}! Good, come here, I wanted a word.
{greet}! You heard me, then. Mampir sebentar, ya.
Ah, {raka}. Nobody stops any more, but you did.

greet.callout.t: Oh! I didn't think you'd really come over. {greet}, {raka}.

greet.memory.heard_good: Ah, the famous {raka}. {other} won't stop talking about you.
{greet}. I hear from {other} that you're settling in well.
So you're the one {other} keeps mentioning. {greet}, {raka}!
{other} told me about you. All good things, don't worry.
greet.memory.heard_bad: Hm. {other} had words about you, you know.
{greet}. {other} wasn't very happy with you, I hear.
Ah, {raka}. I've been hearing things. From {other}.
{greet}. Is it true what {other} says about you?
overhear.raka_good: ...you know Mbah Minah's grandson? Good boy, that one.
...{raka} came by the other day. He listens, you know? Rare.
...no, no, {raka} is fine. Better than fine.
...I told you, {raka} is one of us now.
...Mbah Minah would be proud of that boy.
overhear.raka_bad: ...I don't know about that {raka}. Something's off.
...Mbah Minah's grandson? Hmph. Don't get me started.
...{raka} said what? To me, he's never said anything nice.
overhear.raka_new: ...someone's living in Mbah Minah's house again, you know.
...have you met the new one on Gang Mawar? Mbah Minah's grandson.
...a designer, they say. What does a designer even do?
...Mbah Minah's cucu came back from the city. Finally.
...he hasn't said hello to me yet, that new one.
overhear.other_good: ...you know {other} helped me again last week?
...if everyone were like {other}, this kampung would be heaven.
...I've known {other} for years. Never a bad word.
overhear.other_bad: ...don't mention {other} to me. I'm still angry.
...{other} still hasn't said sorry, you know.
...I'm not saying {other} is a bad person. I'm just saying.
...ask {other} yourself, see what excuse you get this time.
overhear.small: ...prices at the pasar, astaga. Cabai again!
...hot today, eh? The rain should come soon.
...my son says the same thing. Kids these days.
...hahaha! No, really, that's what he said!
...so I said, why not {topic}? And she laughed.
...is the arisan this week or next week?
...ya sudah, see you at the warung.
overhear.ambient: ...the bus was late again this morning.
...this kampung is so clean. Not like ours.
...I only came for the bakso, honestly.
...my cousin lives on Gang Melati, you know.
...the pasar here is cheaper, that's why I come.
callout.stranger: Mas! You're Mbah Minah's cucu, right? Mampir!
Eh, the new neighbour! Mau ke mana, Mas?
You must be the one from Mbah Minah's house. Sini!
Mau ke mana, Mas? Stop for a minute!

callout.stranger.t: Oh... hello? Are you Mbah Minah's grandson?

callout.acquaintance: {raka}! Mau ke mana? Sini, sit a while.
Mau ke mana, {raka}? In such a hurry!

callout.acquaintance.t: Oi, {raka}! Too good to say hello now?

callout.friend: Oi, {raka}! Come sit, I made too much tea again.
Mau ke mana, {raka}? Sit with me first!

callout.friend.t: Mas Raka! I have gossip. Big gossip!

passerby.elder: Ah, {greet}. Young people still greet, how nice.
passerby.young: Kak! Is the bakso cart here tonight?
passerby.again: We keep running into each other.
invite.yes: Oh, with pleasure. {detail}, then. Don't be late!
Siap! {item} {detail}. I'll hold you to it.

invite.yes.t: Oh! Um, yes. Yes, I'd like that. {detail}.

invite.no: Hmm, I'm not sure. Let me think about it. Another day, ya.
Not this time. But thank you for asking.
Aduh, I'm a bit tired lately. Next time, ya?
Maybe when we know each other a little better, hehe.

invite.no.t: No. Ask me again when you're not so new.

invite.busy: {detail}? Aduh, I can't, I'm busy then.
Oh, I'd love to, but not {detail}. I have things on.
{detail} is bad for me. Another day?
Can't, {raka}. Work. Or something like work.
invite.young: Hehe, my mother won't let me, Kak.
I'm too young for that, Kak! Ask my parents.
Ibu says no going out at night, Kak.
Aaah I want to, but I'm not allowed.
Kak, I'd get in trouble! Ask me for something else.
invite.again: You already asked me today, {raka}! Hehe.
Pelan-pelan, {raka}. One invitation a day is plenty.
Again? Let's see how the first one goes.
Hehe, you're keen. Ask me tomorrow.
invite.stranger: Ha, slow down. Let's get to know each other first.
Hmm, maybe once we've talked a bit more.
You're very forward for a new neighbour.
Invite me? I don't even know you yet!
plan.met.kopi: You came! Pak Slamet, two kopi tubruk!
Duduk, duduk. The kopi's on its way.
Ah, good. I hate drinking kopi alone.
There you are. Now we can talk properly.
plan.met.bakso: {raka}! Mas Joko's broth is extra good tonight.
Just in time. I already told Mas Joko you're coming.
Here you are. Nothing beats bakso at night, ya?
Ah, good. I was getting hungry waiting!
plan.met.walk: {greet}! Look at the kali, so calm this early.
You're up! I thought you city people slept till noon.
Ayo, let's walk. The air is best now.
There you are. Listen, the birds!
plan.met.sore: {raka}! Look at the kids. We were like that once.
You came! Best time of day, sore.
Sit here. Watch the sky go orange.
Ah, {raka}. Nice and cool now, ya?
You made it. I saved you a seat.
plan.met.teh: Nice teras. Mbah Minah used to sit right here.
Wah, so this is your place now. It feels like hers still.
I haven't sat on this teras in years.
word.good.warm: Oh? You think so about {other}? Well... that's nice to hear.
Hmm. Maybe I should talk to {other} more.
You think so? I'll keep that in mind.
That's kind of you to say, {raka}.
word.good.agree: Of course! {other} is one of the best people here.
You don't have to tell me. I love {other}.
Ha, we agree on that. {other} is wonderful.
word.good.grudge: {other}, a good person? ...Well. I suppose people change.
Don't try to fix it, {raka}. ...But I heard you.
{other}? I'm still angry. But thank you for telling me.
Hm. That doesn't sound like the {other} I know. But fine.
word.good.stranger: And who are you to tell me about {other}?
Hmm. You don't know the history.
Let's leave that for when we know each other.
word.good.again: You're very busy fixing everyone today, {raka}.
Yes, yes, I heard you the first time.
One piece of advice a day is enough, hehe.
Tomorrow, {raka}. Let me think about today's first.
word.bad.juicy: No! {other} did that? Tell me everything.
Aduh, I knew it! I knew it about {other}!
Wah wah wah. Wait until Bu Ratna hears this.
word.bad.disapprove: {raka}. We don't talk about neighbours like that.
That's not kind. {other} isn't here to answer.
Hm. I'd rather not hear that, {raka}.
Careful. Words travel fast in a kampung.
word.bad.uneasy: Oh... {other}? I don't know about that.
Hmm. Maybe. I'd rather not get involved.
Ya... well. Everyone has their moments.
I didn't need to know that, {raka}.
word.bad.again: More? That's enough gossip for one day.
{raka}, you're worse than Bu Endang today.
Stop, stop. My ears are full.
plate.empty: Oh, the plate! You didn't have to rush.
Ah, my plate. I was wondering where it went, hehe.
Thank you. Next time I'll make extra.
Good, good. Did you finish it all?
plate.full: And you put {item} on it! You know the proper way, {raka}.
Wah, the plate comes back full! Mbah Minah taught you well.
{item} on my plate? Now I owe you again, hehe.
That's how it's done here. Terima kasih, {raka}.
A full plate back. You're a real kampung boy now.
text.group.welcome: Assalamualaikum warga. Please welcome Mas Raka, Mbah Minah's cucu, who has moved into her house on Gang Mawar. Say hello if you see him 🙏
Warga RT 04, we have a new neighbour: Mas Raka, grandson of the late Mbah Minah. Please make him welcome 🙏
text.group.welcome_reply: Wah, Mbah Minah's cucu! Welcome home.
Welcome Mas Raka! The warung is open till late 😄
text.group.ronda: Jadwal ronda malam ini: {detail}. Jangan lupa ya, bapak-bapak 🔦
Ronda tonight: {detail}. Pos ronda from 22:00. Terima kasih 🙏
Reminder: {detail} are on ronda tonight. Stay safe everyone.
Malam ini ronda: {detail}. Kopi is on the RT 😄
text.group.jumat: Jumat berkah, warga. Jumatan at the musholla, please come early 🙏
Reminder: Jumatan today. Ustadz Hasan asks us to come before 11:45.
Selamat hari Jumat. Don't forget Jumatan, bapak-bapak.
text.group.minggu: Selamat pagi warga. Enjoy your Sunday, and please keep the gang clean 🙏
Minggu pagi! Kids, please play at the lapangan, not in the gang 😅
Happy Sunday, warga RT 04. Kerja bakti comes soon, I'll announce the date.
text.group.warung: Warung sudah buka! Gorengan masih panas 🔥
Nasi uduk ready, warga. First come first served 😄
Pagi! Fresh gorengan and teh manis at the warung ☕
Warung open. Telur is cheaper today, stock up 🥚
Pagi warga, warung buka. Kerupuk just delivered!
text.group.chatter: Who else thinks it's going to rain this afternoon? 🌧️
Cabai at the pasar is expensive again 😩
Has anyone seen a grey cat? She hasn't come home since yesterday 🐈
Hahaha did everyone hear the motorbike at 2am? 🙄
Anyone going to the pasar tomorrow? Titip bawang ya 😅
The mangga at Pak Karyo's are almost ripe, I'm watching 👀
Who's got a spare ladder? Mine is broken.
Selamat sore warga! Hot hot hot today ☀️

text.group.chatter.t: Did you see the sunset tonight? Beautiful 😍
Anyone know what happened at the balai yesterday? Just asking 👀
Is it true someone is opening a minimarket on the main road? 🤔

text.group.feud_motor: Once again, a certain motorbike was revving at midnight on Gang Anggrek. Some of us have to sleep. 😤
Warga, is it too much to ask that motorbikes are pushed, not revved, after 22:00? 🙄
Another night of engine noise. I won't name names. {other} knows.
Pak RT, please remind SOME people about the noise rule.
text.group.feud_loan: Some people borrow money and forget the way to your house 🙃
Just a reminder that a promise is a promise. That's all.
Hutang is hutang, warga. Even between neighbours.
I won't say who. But she knows. 🙃
text.group.calm: Let's talk about it face to face, not here ya 🙏
Aduh, not in the group please 😅
Pak RT, maybe we can discuss at the next meeting?
text.group.peace: Just want to say: {other} and I talked. All is well now 🙏
Terima kasih {other}. Let's forget the old story 🤝
Warga, {other} and I made peace. Mas Raka helped a bit, hehe 🙏
text.invite.kopi: Mas Raka, ngopi at Warkop Berkah {detail}? ☕
Oi, warkop {detail}? Pak Slamet has new pisang goreng.
Free {detail}? Let's ngopi at the warkop.
text.invite.bakso: Craving bakso. {detail} at the cart by the pos ronda, ikut?
Bakso {detail}? I'm buying the es teh 😄
text.invite.walk: {raka}, jalan pagi {detail}? By the kali, meet at the bridge 🌅
Walk by the kali {detail}? Good for the body, hehe.
Morning walk {detail}? Meet at the jembatan.
text.invite.sore: Sore at the lapangan {detail}? Watch the kids play 😄
{raka}, lapangan {detail}? The breeze is nice there.
Sit at the lapangan {detail}? I'll bring kacang.
Free {detail}? Let's sit at the lapangan bench.
text.declined: Ya sudah, no problem. Next time!
text.missed: Where were you? I sat at {detail} for ages.
I guess you forgot about {detail}. It's okay.
You didn't come to {detail}. Is everything alright?
text.expired: No answer, so I guess not. Next time ya!
Okay, maybe you're busy. Another day!
I'll take that as a no 😄
text.hello: {raka}! This is my number, save it ya 😄
Halo {raka}, it's me. Now you can't say you don't have my number 😄
Assalamualaikum {raka}. Save my number, in case you need anything 🙏
Hi! Saved you as "Mas Raka Mbah Minah" hehe
It's me! Message me any time.
text.plate: {raka}, I left some {item} on your teras. Still warm! 😊
Made too much {item}, there's a plate by your door 🙏
There's {item} by your door. Bring the plate back whenever, no rush 😄
For the new neighbour: {item}. On your teras!
text.plate_remind: {raka}, no rush about the plate hehe. Just saying 😄
Did you like it? The plate is the blue one, by the way 😅
If you're passing by, bring the plate ya 🙏
